JSON must serialize (floats and None are fine). Commit the generated JSON files too. TESTS (tests/test_enforce_stage1_harness.py, no network, reading files only; plus the extension in tests/test_live_baseline_enforce.py using its existing fake-Worker pattern): a) the script text carries port 8795, `--enforce`, not `--shadow`, `enforce-stage1`, `--max-calls 70` and `0.03` for smoke, `--max-calls 700` and `0.20` for full, and none of `shadow-sample`, `8793`, `8794`; b) the generated manifests equal the committed JSON files byte for byte (run the generator into a temp dir or compare its in-memory output) and carry only this stage's paths and numbers (no `shadow-sample3`, `topup`); c) the runner spec contains the foreground rule and the preregistration path; d) the check strings contain 30000 / 200000, `enforce`, `turn_elapsed_s`; e) in live_baseline tests: with `--enforce` a turn whose verifier is called twice (stub ask: first reply rejects, second accepts) yields two `enforce_attempts` with the schema keys, `accepted` False then True, rows JSON-serializable, `turn_elapsed_s` a float; a turn with no relations yields `[]`; with `--enforce` off the rows have neither key. Keep each test short and independent.

It plays the frozen route `observe_topup` (9 commands) through `scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/live_baseline.py --enforce` against a local capped Worker. Row schema of an enforced run (rows.json is a list of replicates, each {route, opening, turns:[row]}); a turn row has these keys, among others already written today: `input` (str), `narration` (str, or None when the turn FAILED), `error` (str or None; set when the turn failed and the engine rolled the world back), `places_before` and `places_after` (dicts), `narration_attempts` (int, narrator calls this turn; 0 for an engine-authored turn), `verifier_requests` (int), `observation_enforce` (dict with `observation_preview` and/or `observation_diverged` keys, or None), `provider_responses` (list of raw reply strings of this turn, in order). A turn whose preview needed no verifier call has an empty list. YOUR TASK: the stage-1 report script. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY these NEW files: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/enforce_report.py and tests/test_enforce_report.py. Do NOT edit shadow_report.py (read it fully first and mirror its CLI conventions, its label-file format idea, its hashing/printing style and its blind-sheet style). BUILD `enforce_report.py` with three subcommands: `labels-template ROWS`, `sheet ROWS`, `join ROWS --labels LABELS` (each takes the path of rows.json; `--out` optional like shadow_report). A turn id is `r<replicate>t<turn>` (0-based). SHEET (blind): one block per turn in a deterministic shuffled order (fixed seed written into the output header; the shuffle must not reveal replicate order). For each turn show: the turn id, the command, the THINGS the engine required (union of `relations` of the last `enforce_attempts` entry: thing, plus place when present, and `held` when the thing's holder is set; or `(none)` when the list is empty), and the narration: the committed `narration`, or the line `no narration: the turn did not complete`. For a turn that needed recovery (`narration_attempts` >= 2, or `error` set with at least one attempt) ALSO show each REJECTED earlier attempt as `earlier attempt 1`, `earlier attempt 2` (text from `enforce_attempts[i].narration` for attempts the verifier rejected; if `narration_attempts` exceeds the verifier-call count, show the extra attempts from `provider_responses` as `earlier raw reply`, best effort: take the `segments` text if the reply parses as JSON, else the raw string). The sheet must NOT contain any verifier score, verdict, outcome, `accepted`, request count, attempt count, error text or the word enforce, and must not mark which narration was committed beyond the labels above. Add a test that scans the sheet for those leaks. LABELS: a JSON file keyed by turn id: {turn_id: {presents_required: bool|null, acceptable: bool|null, tags: {refind, invented_object, leak, wrong_custody, unrequested_move: bool|null}, earlier: [bool|null, ...]}}, where `earlier[i]` is `really_deficient` for the i-th earlier attempt shown. `labels-template` writes one entry per turn with every value null and `earlier` sized to the number of earlier attempts. A null label is 'missing' and a join with missing labels for observation turns prints MISSING LABELS with the turn ids and exits 1 (null tags are not missing, like in shadow_report; a failed turn needs no `presents_required` or `acceptable`). JOIN: print a Markdown report, the labels file sha256 and the rows sha256, a per-turn table (turn id, command, attempts, verifier requests, elapsed, outcome: committed, recovered or FAILED), and these clauses, each PASS, FAIL or INCONCLUSIVE with the counts used. An OBSERVATION turn is a turn with a non-empty `enforce_attempts` or `observation_enforce` not None. A FAILED turn is one with `error` set and `narration` None. A RECOVERED turn has `narration_attempts` >= 2 and a narration. Clause 1: observation turns that end FAILED, at most 1; print the count, n, and the one-sided 95% Wilson upper bound. Clause 2: committed narrations (observation turns, not failed) whose label `presents_required` is false: must be 0. FAIL stops the line with the text `STOP: the verifier let deficient prose through`. Clause 3: committed narrations tagged leak, wrong_custody or unrequested_move: must be 0; tagged refind: at most 1; tagged invented_object: at most 1 (report each tag separately). Clause 4 (rollback): for every FAILED turn, `places_after == places_before`, `narration` is None, `error` is set, and the NEXT turn of that replicate (if any) has no error caused by the previous one (just report whether the next row exists and ran); zero violations. Clause 5 (budget): no turn with `narration_attempts` > 2 or `verifier_requests` > 2 (a verifier request is a model request; `verifier_requests` already sums them); zero violations. Clause 6 (latency): among turns with `narration_attempts` == 1 and no error, p95 of `turn_elapsed_s` at most 10.0 s (nearest-rank percentile; say how); print p50 and p95 for them and, separately, p50 and max for recovered turns; INCONCLUSIVE when fewer than 20 such turns. Clause 7 (false rejects): over all earlier attempts the verifier rejected (an attempt is rejected when its entry is not accepted), those labelled not `really_deficient` must be at most 1; INCONCLUSIVE when fewer than 5 rejected attempts. INFORMATION lines (never gated): first-attempt rejection rate (observation turns with `narration_attempts` >= 2 or FAILED, over observation turns); recovery success rate (recovered over turns that needed recovery); total narration attempts and verifier requests; mean `turn_elapsed_s` of observation turns; the share of observation turns with `observation_diverged` true; and, for the two shadow-sample defect clauses, `refind` tags on `feel under the drawer` turns and `invented_object` tags on `inspect the passenger seat` turns (the only story strings allowed, as named constants like REFIND_COMMAND in shadow_report.py). Overall line: `enforcement screen: PASS` only when clauses 1 to 6 are PASS (INCONCLUSIVE counts as not PASS and is printed as such) and clause 7 is PASS or INCONCLUSIVE. TESTS (tests/test_enforce_report.py; build synthetic rows in the test as plain dicts following the schema above; no real rows needed): a clean run passes; a FAILED turn with correct rollback passes clause 4, one with changed places fails it; a recovered turn (two enforce_attempts, first rejected) appears with its earlier attempt on the sheet and counts in the information lines; each clause has a test that violates it and prints FAIL (1 with two FAILED turns, 2 with presents_required false and the STOP text, 3 per tag, 5 with three attempts, 6 with slow turns and with too few turns for INCONCLUSIVE, 7 with two false rejects); missing labels exit 1; the sheet leak scan; the shuffle is deterministic and the seed is printed; the template shape. Keep each test short.
